title: Harsher on Male? Evaluating LLMs on Gender-Asymmetric Moral Framing in Conflicts
lede: An arXiv paper introduces GAMA-Bench, 1,298 gender-mirrored conflict scenarios, and finds that 10 LLMs frame the same misconduct more punitively when the person at fault is a man.

points: Each scenario starts as a gender-neutral misconduct template, then becomes paired first-person prompts that swap only the actor's gender and role references.
The scenarios cover intimate relationships and public social conflicts.
Responses are scored on how they distribute punishment, empathy, escalation, instruction and blame.
Male actors draw more blame and escalation; female actors get more therapeutic, empathetic framing for the same behaviour.
The gap holds across model families, model sizes, scenario types and explicit reasoning modes, and the code is published.

points.text: Most commenters are unsurprised and read the result as a mirror of training data and current social norms.
Others doubt data is the whole story and point to the alignment phase as a likely source of the skew.
One commenter wonders whether men are also praised more for good outcomes, or whether the gap shows only in negative cases.
